para.text: An applicant shall submit:
A completed application to the Board on the form that the Board requires;
To a criminal history records check (CHRC) in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8–303, Annotated Code of Maryland;
Written evidence satisfactory to the Board that the applicant has submitted to a CHRC as required by §A(2) of this regulation by submitting:
One complete set of fingerprints, as required by the Central Repository and the FBI; and
All fees required by the Central Repository and the FBI;

Any documentation requested from the applicant by the Board including, but not limited to, official certified or true test court documents and a signed, dated explanation written by the applicant, regarding the facts and circumstances, outcome, and current status of any criminal history record information received by the Board:
Under Health Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland;
In an answer to a question on the Board’s application form; or
From any other source; and
Any additional documentation requested by the Board if the documentation received from the applicant under §A(4) this regulation is incomplete or insufficient.
If an application is not complete when initially submitted to the Board by the applicant, the applicant shall have no longer than 12 months from the date the application is received by the Board to:
Complete the application; and
Provide all information and documents required in §A of this regulation.

If an applicant fails to provide to the Board a complete application and any additional documentation requested by the Board in §A of this regulation within 12 months from the date the application is received by the Board, then the application:
Shall be considered abandoned; and
May be destroyed.
Once an application is deemed abandoned under §C of this regulation, an individual seeking licensure shall:
Submit a new application;
Meet all of the requirements for licensure; and
Pay the required fees that are in effect at the time of re-application.

para.text: The Board shall place the license of any registered nurse or licensed practical nurse on inactive status if the licensee:

Has not satisfactorily completed 1,000 hours of active nursing practice or graduated from an approved nursing program within the 5-year period immediately preceding the date of anticipated renewal or chooses inactive status;
Completes the biennial application for inactive status; and
Pays all fees.

A licensee on inactive status may not practice nursing in this State. However, a registered nurse on inactive status may use the title “registered nurse”, and a practical nurse on inactive status may use the title “licensed practical nurse”.
A licensee on inactive status may apply for an active status license provided that the licensee:
Meets the renewal requirements of Health Occupations Article, §8-312, Annotated Code of Maryland; and
Submits to the Board:
The required application; and
Written, verified evidence that the licensee has submitted to a criminal history records check in accordance with Regulation .13 of this chapter by:
Submitting one complete set of fingerprints required by the Central Repository and the FBI; and
Paying all fees required by the Central Repository and the FBI.
An additional fee may not be charged to change from inactive to active status.

para.text: In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“Board” means the Board of Nursing.

“Board-approved course” means an educational offering specific to the case management of the injured worker under the Workers' Compensation Commission which meets the criteria established by the Board.
“Central Repository” has the meaning stated in COMAR 10.27.01.01.
“Commission” means the Workers' Compensation Commission.
“Criminal history records check (CHRC)” has the meaning stated in COMAR 10.27.01.01.
Medical Case Management.

“Medical case management” means any type of contact, including electronic, written, and personal, with the injured worker, for the purpose of the planning and coordination of health services appropriate to achievement of medical rehabilitation of the injured worker.
“Medical case management” includes but is not limited to:
Case assessment;
Implementation and coordination of services with the injured worker, family, and health care providers;
Evaluation of treatment results;
Coordinating community re-entry;
Return to work with the employer of injury; and
Referral for further vocational rehabilitation services.
“Medical claims consultant” means a registered nurse who consults on medical aspects of an injured worker's rehabilitation without any contact with the injured worker.
“Multistate licensure privilege” has the meaning set forth in COMAR 10.27.01.01B.
“Registered nurse (RN)” means an individual who:
Is licensed by the Board to practice registered nursing; or
Has a multistate licensure privilege to practice registered nursing.
“RN-WCCM” means a registered nurse-workers' compensation medical case manager.

para.text: For certification as an RN-WCCM, an applicant shall:
Hold a current license to practice registered nursing in this State or a multistate licensure privilege to practice registered nursing;
Submit documentation of successful completion of a Board-approved course;
Submit to the Board a completed application for certification as an RN-WCCM;
Pay all fees; and
Submit to a criminal history records check (CHRC) in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland.
The Board shall include on the RN's license the designation WCCM.
Certification by Endorsement. An applicant from out-of-State shall meet the requirements as stated in this regulation.
Unless renewed biennially, a certification to practice as an RN-WCCM expires at the same time as the registered nurse license.
Before certification as an RN-WCCM expires, the RN-WCCM may renew the certification for an additional term, if the RN—WCCM:
Is otherwise entitled to be certified;
Has practiced a minimum of 2,000 hours in the past 2 years as an RN—WCCM;
Submits a completed application for renewal on the form the Board requires;
Pays all fees; and
If required to submit to a CHRC in accordance with §E of this regulation, submits written evidence satisfactory to the Board that the applicant has submitted to a CHRC by submitting:
One complete set of fingerprints, as required by the Central Repository and the FBI; and
All fees required by the Central Repository and the FBI.

If the registered nurse does not meet the practice requirement stated in §B(2) of this regulation, the registered nurse shall complete a Board-approved course to be eligible for renewal of the RN-WCCM certification.
Upon notification by the Board that a CHRC is required before the certification can be renewed, a renewal applicant shall comply with all of the requirements under §B of this regulation.
Criminal history records checks for renewal applicants shall be scheduled according to the certification holder’s birth month as follows:
In 2026 — all applicants with a September or October birth month;
In 2027 — all applicants with an October or November birth month;
In 2028 — all applicants with a November or December birth month;
In 2029 — all applicants with a December or January birth month;
In 2030 — all applicants with a January or February birth month;
In 2031 — all applicants with a February or March birth month;
In 2032 — all applicants with a March or April birth month;
In 2033 — all applicants with an April or May birth month;
In 2034 — all applicants with a May or June birth month;
In 2035 — all applicants with a June or July birth month.
In 2036 — all applicants with a July or August birth month; and
In 2037— all applicants with an August or September birth month.

For renewal applicants who are required to submit a CHRC, the Board may not renew a certification without written documentation that the applicant has submitted to a CHRC in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland.

section.heading: Exceptions.
section.text: This chapter does not apply to an individual who:

para.text: Other than a certified nursing assistant, practices a health occupation, that the individual is authorized to practice under the Health Occupations Article, Annotated Code of Maryland;
Provides for the gratuitous care of friends, domestic partners, or family members;
Performs nursing assistant tasks while a nursing student enrolled in an accredited nursing program if the individual either:
Is practicing under the direct supervision of qualified faculty or preceptors; or

Successfully completed the portion of the approved nursing education program that the Board determines meets the requirements of an approved nursing assistant training program as described in Regulation .05D of this chapter;
Performs nursing assistant tasks:
While a student enrolled in an approved nursing assistant training program or approved acute care nursing assistant training program; and
While practicing under the direct supervision of qualified faculty or preceptors;
Practices as a certified nursing assistant-I for less than 4 months in accordance with 42 CFR §483.35(d);
Performs nursing tasks delegated by a registered nurse or licensed practical nurse so long as the delegated nursing tasks do not become a routine part of the individual's job duties;
Performs nursing tasks delegated by an advanced practice registered nurse in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-02(d), Annotated Code of Maryland; or
Performs technical tasks delegated by a licensed certified midwife in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-02(e), Annotated Code of Maryland.
In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“Acute care nursing assistant training program” means a course of training that meets the acute care nursing assistant training program curriculum approved by the Board.
“Board” means the Maryland Board of Nursing.
“Central Repository” means the Maryland Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository of the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
“Certificate” means a certificate issued by the Board to practice as a certified nursing assistant in the State.
Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA).
“Certified nursing assistant (CNA)” means an individual, regardless of title, who, for compensation and subject to regulations adopted by the Board, routinely performs:
Nursing tasks delegated by a registered nurse, licensed practical nurse, or advanced practice registered nurse; or
Technical tasks delegated by a licensed certified midwife.
“Certified nursing assistant (CNA)” does not include dialysis technician or medication technician.
Certified Nursing Assistant-I (CNA-I).
“Certified nursing assistant-I (CNA-I)” means a CNA who:
Meets the requirements set by the Board and federal law; and
May practice in any practice setting.
“Certified nursing assistant-I (CNA-I)” includes a:
CNA who was certified as a geriatric nursing assistant on March 31, 2026;
Certified medicine aide; and
CNA who is certified under Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-05(c)(5), Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Certified nursing assistant-II (CNA-II)” means a CNA who:
On March 31, 2026, was certified as a CNA but not certified as a geriatric nursing assistant; and
May not practice in a nursing facility or skilled nursing facility.

“Criminal history records check (CHRC)” means the performance of both a State criminal history records check by the Central Repository and a national criminal history records check performed by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).

“Criminal history record information” means information provided by the criminal history records check regarding an applicant’s criminal arrests, charges, and convictions and other dispositions of criminal charges.
“Good standing” means without an encumbrance that limits or restricts practice, such as revocation, suspension, or probation.
“Nursing assistant competency evaluation” means an examination approved by the Board that:
Determines the competency of the individual to practice as a CNA-I; and
Meets the requirements under federal law.
“Nursing assistant training program” means a course of training approved by the Board that meets the requirements under federal and State law.
“Service member” has the meaning stated in State Government Article, §9-901, Annotated Code of Maryland.

“Temporary nurse aide” means an individual who practiced as a geriatric nursing assistant without certification during the national Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) Public Health Emergency, as declared on January 31, 2020, and periodically continued by the United States Secretary of Health and Human Services, pursuant to the waiver of the requirements of 42 CFR §483.35(d) issued by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services on March 6, 2020.
“Technical task” means a routine clinical act or task that does not require clinical judgment and is performed with the supervision as specified in COMAR 10.69.02.
“Temporary nurse aide training” means an 8-hour online training and examination program offered by:
The American Health Care Association;
The National Center for Assisted Living; or
Another comparable program approved by the Board.
Fees are as follows:
Initial certification fee — $20;
Endorsement fee — $20;
Renewal fee — $40;
Verification of certification to another jurisdiction — $25;
Returned check fee — $25;
Duplicate certificate fee — $10.
Fees are not refundable.
An applicant shall submit:
A completed application to the Board on the form that the Board requires;
To a CHRC in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland;
Written evidence satisfactory to the Board that the applicant has submitted to a CHRC as required by §A(2) of this regulation by submitting:
One complete set of fingerprints, as required by the Central Repository and the FBI; and
All fees required by the Central Repository and the FBI;

Any documentation requested from the applicant by the Board including, but not limited to, official certified or true test court documents and a signed, dated explanation written by the applicant, regarding the facts and circumstances, outcome, and current status of any criminal history record information received by the Board:
Under §A(2) of this regulation;
In an answer to a question on the Board’s application form; or
From any other source; and
Any additional documentation requested by the Board if the documentation received from the applicant under §A(4) of this regulation is incomplete or insufficient.

If an application is not complete when initially submitted to the Board by the applicant, the applicant shall have no longer than 12 months from the date the application is received by the Board to complete the application and provide all information and documents required in §A of this regulation.

If an applicant fails to provide to the Board a complete application and any additional documentation requested by the Board under §A of this regulation within 12 months from the date the application is received by the Board, then the application shall be considered abandoned and may be destroyed.

Once an application is deemed abandoned under §C of this regulation, an individual seeking CNA certification shall submit a new application on the form required by the Board and meet all of the requirements for CNA certification and pay the required fees that are in effect at the time of re-application.

para.text: Initial Certification. An applicant for initial nursing assistant certification shall have successfully:
Completed:
An approved nursing assistant training program;
An approved acute care nursing assistant training program;
A portion of an approved nursing education program that has been determined by the Board to meet the requirements of a nursing assistant training program set by the Board; or

Service member training and education that has been determined by the Board to be substantially equivalent to a nursing assistant training program approved by the Board in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §1-702, Annotated Code of Maryland; and
Passed a nursing assistant competency evaluation.
Certification by Endorsement. An applicant for nursing assistant certification by endorsement shall:
Hold a certificate to practice as a nursing assistant that:

Was issued by another state or territory of the United States that has certification requirements that are essentially similar to those set forth in Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-05, Annotated Code of Maryland; and
Is in good standing; and
Have successfully completed a nursing assistant training program that meets the standards for an approved nursing assistant training program set by the Board.
Any applicant for nursing assistant certification may not have:
Committed any act or omission that would be grounds for discipline or denial of certification under Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-10, Annotated Code of Maryland; or

A record of abuse, negligence, or misappropriation of a client's property or any disciplinary action taken or pending in any other state or territory of the United States against the certification of the CNA.
Nursing Education Programs.
To meet the requirements of a nursing assistant training program set by the Board, a portion of a nursing education program must include courses with content that primarily focuses on:
Nursing fundamentals;
Mental health;
Health assessment;
Nursing ethics; and
The content listed under 42 CFR §483.152(b).

If a portion of a nursing education program does not include courses with content that primarily focuses on the subject matters set forth in § D(1) of this regulation, the Board may review and approve other equivalent subject matters as meeting the requirements of a nursing assistant training program set by the Board.
A CNA-II who seeks certification as a CNA-1 shall meet the qualifications set forth in §A of this regulation.
Temporary Nurse Aides.
A temporary nurse aide applying for certification as a CNA-1 shall be deemed to have completed a nursing assistant training program approved by the Board if the temporary nurse aide:
Completed a temporary nurse aide training course;
Completed a minimum of 100 hours of on-the-job training as a temporary nurse aide that:
Met the requirements under 42 CFR §483.152(a) and 42 CFR §483.152(b)(2)—(7); and
Was not provided in a facility described under 42 CFR §483.151(b)(2)—(3); and
In addition to the minimum 100 hours of on-the-job training, worked as a temporary nurse aide competently for a minimum of 160 hours.

A temporary nurse aide whose on-the-job training did not meet all of the requirements under 42 CFR 483.152(a) and 42 CFR 483.152(b)(2)—(7) may receive supplemental training in those requirements and be deemed to meet the requirement of §F(1)(b)(i) of this regulation.
Initial Certification.
An applicant for initial certification shall:
Comply with all of the requirements under Regulation .04A of this chapter;
Pay the required fee to the Board; and
Submit to the Board one of the items in §A(2) of this regulation.
Verification Requirements.

For graduates of a nursing assistant or acute care nursing assistant training program, an application that has been signed by the program coordinator or faculty of the training program completed by the applicant;

For service members, documentation demonstrating successful completion of service member training and education that has been determined by the Board to be substantially equivalent to a nursing assistant training program approved by the Board;

For nursing students and graduates, an official transcript demonstrating successful completion of a portion of an approved nursing education program that the Board determines meets the requirements for a nursing assistant training program set by the Board; or

For foreign-educated nursing graduates, a copy of an evaluation of the applicant’s transcript through a Board-approved vendor demonstrating successful completion of a portion of an approved nursing education program that meets the requirements for a nursing assistant training program set by the Board.
A program coordinator or faculty of a nursing assistant or acute care nursing assistant training program:
May sign an application before graduation; and
Shall submit written verification, as required by the Board, of program completion to the Board after 5 business days of the applicant’s program completion.

An applicant shall submit an application for initial certification after 24 months of the date of completion of an approved nursing assistant training program, an approved acute care nursing assistant training program, or portion of an approved nursing education program.

If an applicant fails to meet §A(4) of this regulation, an applicant still seeking certification shall take or re-take an approved nursing assistant training program or approved acute care nursing assistant training program and comply with §A(4) of this regulation.
Certification by Endorsement. An applicant for nursing assistant certification by endorsement shall:
Comply with all of the requirements under Regulation .04A of this chapter;
Pay the required fee to the Board; and
Submit the following verifications directly to the Board from the appropriate authority:
A certificate to practice as a nursing assistant in good standing from another state or territory with certification requirements that are essentially similar to the requirements in this State; and
A certificate of completion from a nursing assistant training program in that state or territory that meets the standards for an approved nursing assistant training program set by the Board.
Every applicant shall attest on the application whether the applicant has:
Committed any act or omission that would be grounds for discipline or denial of certification; and

A record of abuse, neglect, or misappropriation of a client’s property or any disciplinary action taken or pending in any state or territory of the United States against the certification of the applicant.
A CNA-II who seeks certification as a CNA-I shall:
Submit an application to the Board on the form required by the Board; and
Comply with §§A(1)(c) and A(3)—(5) of this regulation.
A temporary nurse aide applying for certification as a CNA-1 shall:
Comply with §A of this regulation; and
Ensure that the administrator, director of nursing, or human resources representative of the applicant’s employer submits to the Board an attestation, on the form required by the Board, that:
Is completed by the:
Applicant;
Registered Nurse instructor or supervisor of the applicant during employment; and
Administrator or director of nursing for the employer; and
Verifies that the applicant satisfies the requirements of Regulation .05F of this chapter.
An individual is eligible to sit for a nursing assistant competency evaluation if the individual:
Meets the education requirements set forth in Regulation .05A(1) of this chapter; or
Must retake a nursing assistant competency evaluation in order to renew or reinstate a certification in accordance with Regulation .10C(2)(a) of this chapter.

Except for service members, an individual shall sit for a nursing assistant competency evaluation after 24 months of meeting the educational requirements set forth in Regulation .05A(1) of this chapter.

An individual who fails to sit for a nursing assistant competency evaluation after 24 months of meeting the educational qualifications must re-take an approved nursing assistant training program or approved acute care nursing assistant training program in order to be eligible to sit for a nursing assistant competency evaluation.
Re-testing.
An individual who fails to obtain a passing score on the first examination may retake a nursing assistant competency evaluation three additional times.
An individual shall wait at least 45 calendar days from the date of the prior evaluation before retaking a nursing assistant competency evaluation.

An individual who fails to obtain a passing score after taking a nursing assistant competency evaluation four times must complete a new approved nursing assistant training program or approved acute care nursing assistant training program before retaking a nursing assistant competency evaluation.
The Board may issue a temporary practice certificate to an applicant who:
Has met the appropriate certification requirements to the satisfaction of the Board;
Does not have a criminal record; and
Has not been the subject of a health professional disciplinary action in this State or another jurisdiction.
Unless the Board suspends or revokes a temporary practice certificate, the temporary practice certificate expires 90 calendar days after the date of issuance.
A temporary practice certificate may be extended up to an additional 90 calendar days if the applicant is awaiting the completion of the criminal history records check.
The Board may not issue a certificate to an applicant until the Board has:
Received and reviewed the criminal history record information of the applicant; and
Approved the application.

Unless subject to discipline, the Board shall issue a certificate to each applicant who meets all the requirements of this chapter and Health Occupations Article, §§8-6A-05 and 8-6A-06, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Expiration.
Unless renewed for an additional two-year term, and except as otherwise provided in §A(2) of this regulation, a certificate expires in accordance with the following schedule:
The certificate of a certificate holder with an odd-numbered birth year expires on the 28th day of the certificate holder’s birth month in an odd-numbered year; and
The certificate of a certificate holder with an even-numbered birth year expires on the 28th day of the certificate holder’s birth month in an even-numbered year.
A certificate shall not expire within 180 calendar days of the date of issuance.
Renewal Notice.
At least 3 months before a certificate expires, the Board shall send the certificate holder a renewal notice by either:
First-class mail to the last known address of the certificate holder; or
Electronic means to the last known electronic address of the certificate holder.
The renewal notice shall provide:
The date on which the certificate holder’s certificate is scheduled to expire;

The date by which the Board must receive a renewal application in order for a certificate to remain active until the renewal application submitted by the certificate holder is processed by the Board, in accordance with State Government Article, §10-226(b), Annotated Code of Maryland;
The amount of the renewal fee; and
If the certificate holder is required to submit to a CHRC in accordance with §D of this regulation:
Notice that the certificate holder must submit to a CHRC in order to renew the certificate; and
Written instructions for how to complete a CHRC.
It is the responsibility of the certificate holder to:
Be aware of the expiration date of the certificate; and
Renew the certificate before it expires.
Failure of a certificate holder to receive the renewal notice sent by the Board does not relieve the certificate holder of the responsibility to renew a certificate before it expires.
Renewal Requirements.
The Board shall renew a certificate if the individual applying for renewal:
Is otherwise entitled to be certified;
Submits a complete application for renewal on the form required by the Board;
Pays the renewal fee;

Provides satisfactory evidence, as required by the Board, of16 hours of active employment, for compensation, as a nursing assistant within the 2-year period immediately preceding the date of expiration or meet the requirements under §C(2) of this regulation; and
If required to submit to a CHRC in accordance with § D of this regulation, complies with the requirements of Regulation .04A of this chapter.
If the individual applying for renewal does not have 16 hours of active employment as a nursing assistant within the 2-year period immediately preceding the date of expiration the individual shall:
If a CNA-I, take and pass a nursing assistant competency evaluation; or
If a CNA-II, complete a nursing assistant training program..
Schedule for CHRCs. CHRCs for renewal applicants shall be scheduled according to the certificate holder’s birth month as follows:
In 2025 — all applicants with an August or September birth month;
In 2026 — all applicants with a September or October birth month;
In 2027 — all applicants with an October or November birth month;
In 2028 — all applicants with a November or December birth month;
In 2029 — all applicants with a December or January birth month;
In 2030 — all applicants with a January or February birth month;
In 2031 — all applicants with a February or March birth month;
In 2032 — all applicants with a March or April birth month;
In 2033 — all applicants with an April or May birth month;
In 2034 — all applicants with a May or June birth month;
In 2035 — all applicants with a June or July birth month; and
In 2036 — all applicants with a July or August birth month.
Grace Period. A certificate holder has a 30 calendar day grace period beyond the expiration date of the certificate to renew the certificate.

The Board shall reinstate the certificate of a certificate holder who has failed to renew the certificate for any reason, if the certificate holder meets the renewal requirements in Health Occupations Article, §8-6A-08, Annotated Code of Maryland, and Regulation .10 of this chapter.
An applicant for administrative reinstatement who has failed to renew the certificate for a period of 1 year or more shall submit to a CHRC before the certificate is reinstated.

para.text: In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“Board” means the Maryland Board of Nursing.
“Central Repository” has the meaning stated in COMAR 10.39.01.02.
“Certificate” means a certificate issued by the Board to practice as a certified medication technician in this State.
Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA).
“Certified nursing assistant (CNA)” means an individual, regardless of title, who:
Routinely performs delegated nursing tasks which were delegated by a registered nurse (RN) or licensed practice nurse (LPN) for compensation; and
Is certified under COMAR 10.39.01.
“Certified nursing assistant (CNA)” does not include:
A medication technician; or
An individual who merely provides assistance with activities of daily living unless the client's needs are such that adverse health consequences are predictable.
“Clinical refresher course” means a course of study approved by the Board to maintain the medication technician's knowledge and skill to administer medication.
“Criminal history records check (CHRC)” has the meaning stated in COMAR 10.39.01.02.
“Licensed practical nurse (LPN)” means an individual who:
Is licensed by the Board to practice licensed practical nursing; or
Has a multistate licensure privilege to practice licensed practical nursing.
“Medication technician (MT)” means an individual who:
Has successfully completed a Board-approved MT training program;
Meets any other qualifications set by the Board; and
Is certified by the Board as a MT.

“Medication technician training program” means a course of training approved by the Board that meets the basic MT core curriculum and content training specific to the setting in which the MT will work.
“Multistate licensure privilege” has the meaning set forth in COMAR 10.27.01.01B.
“Registered nurse (RN)” means an individual who:
Is licensed by the Board to practice registered nursing; or
Has a multistate licensure privilege to practice registered nursing.

para.text: An applicant for MT certification shall:
Be 18 years old or older; and
Submit to the Board:
An application to the Board on the form required by the Board and signed by the RN that taught the applicant's medication technician training program; and
The required fee;
Be of good moral character; and
Submit to a criminal history records check (CHRC) in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland.
An applicant for MT certification may not have:
Committed any act or omission that would be grounds for discipline or denial of certification under this subtitle; or

A record of abuse, negligence, misappropriation of a resident's property, or any disciplinary action taken or pending in any state or territory of the United States against any certificate or license issued to the applicant.
An applicant for MT certification from any other state, territory, or country shall meet all requirements of this chapter.
An applicant for MT certification shall provide:

Any documentation requested from the applicant by the Board including, but not limited to, official certified or true test court documents and a signed, dated explanation written by the applicant, regarding the facts and circumstances, outcome, and current status of any criminal history record information received by the Board:
Under §A(4) of this regulation;
In an answer to a question on the Board’s application form;
From any other source; and

para.text: Term. A license issued pursuant to Health Occupations Article, §8-6B-12, Annotated Code of Maryland, authorizes the licensee to practice licensed electrology while the license is active.

Expiration. Unless renewed, a license expires on the 28th day of a licensee's birth month of every odd-numbered year, except that an initial license shall not expire within 180 days of the date of issuance.
A licensee otherwise entitled to be licensed shall renew a license for 2 years by submitting to the Board:
A renewal application on a form provided by the Board;
The applicable fee as set forth in COMAR 10.53.12; and
Evidence acceptable to the Board of completion of the CEU requirement as set forth in COMAR 10.53.04.

On notification by the Board that a criminal history records check is required before renewal of licensure, a renewal applicant shall comply with all requirements under Regulation .01A of this chapter.
Criminal history records checks (CHRCs) for renewal applicants shall be scheduled according to the licensee’s birth month as follows:
In 2027 — all applicants with a September and October birth month;
In 2029 — all applicants with a November and December birth month;
In 2031 — all applicants with a January and February birth month;
In 2033 — all applicants with a March and April birth month;
In 2035 — all applicants with a May and June birth month; and
In 2037 — all applicants with a July and August birth month.

After notification to the licensee at the address provided to the Board that a criminal history records check is required for renewal, the Board may not renew a license without written documentation that the applicant has submitted to a criminal history records check in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland.

para.text: The Board shall place a license on inactive status if the licensee:
Submits to the Board:
A written request for inactive status; and
The applicable one-time fee as set forth in COMAR 10.53.12; or
Fails to submit the number of CEUs required for renewal of licensure as set forth in COMAR 10.53.04.
The Board shall reactivate a license if:
The license has been inactive for less than 5 years;
The licensee is otherwise entitled to be licensed; and
The licensee submits to the Board:
A reactivation application on a form required by the Board;
Evidence of completion of 10 CEUs for each year before application;
The renewal fee as set forth in COMAR 10.53.12; and
Written, verified evidence that the applicant for reactivation of their license has completed an application for a criminal history records check by submitting the following:
One complete set of fingerprints, as required by the Central Repository and the FBI; and
All fees required by the Central Repository and the FBI.
A license may not be reactivated until the Board has:
Received and reviewed the criminal history records information; and
Approved the application.
If a license has been inactive for 5 years or more, the individual shall successfully take the Board-approved theory and clinical electrology examinations.

While on inactive status an electrologist or electrology instructor is not authorized to practice or instruct and may not use the designation “Electrologist”, “Licensed Electrologist”, “Electrology Instructor”, “Licensed Electrology Instructor”, “L.E.”, or “L.E.I.”.

One complete set of fingerprints, as required by the Central Repository and the FBI; and
All fees required by the Central Repository and the FBI.
A license may not be issued until the Board has:
Received and reviewed the criminal history records information; and
Approved the application.
An electrology instructor license that has been inactive or lapsed may be reinstated if the electrologist is:
Otherwise entitled to be licensed; and
Meets the requirements of Regulation .08B of this chapter.

An electrologist or electrology instructor whose license has been expired for 5 years or more may become licensed if the individual meets the current requirements for initial licensure by examination.

section.heading: Term and Renewal of License and Reinstatement of License.

para.text: A license issued under this regulation authorizes the licensee to practice direct-entry midwifery while the license is active.
A license:
Expires on the 28th day of a licensee's birth month of every odd-numbered year, except that an initial license shall not expire within 180 days of the date of issuance;
Is valid for 2 years, except for an initial license issued before the next renewal date;
Issued for less than the full 2-year period shall be renewed at the next annual renewal date; and
May be renewed for an additional term if the applicant:
Meets the renewal requirements under §B(4)(c) of this regulation:
Pays to the Board a renewal fee specified in Regulation 18 of this chapter; and
Submits to the Board:
A renewal application on the form that the Board requires; and
Satisfactory evidence of compliance with any continuing education or other competency requirements for license renewal.
In addition to all other qualifications and requirements established by the Board for license renewal, the renewal applicant shall submit proof of completion of:
20 accredited and Board-approved continuing education units to be completed in the 2 years preceding the renewal date;
4 hours of peer review in the 2 years before the renewal date in accordance with NARM standards for official peer review; and
Submission of the annual reports required under Regulation .12 of this chapter.
The Board shall renew the license of each licensee who meets the requirements of this regulation.
A renewal applicant shall be placed on inactive status if the licensee:
Fails to provide satisfactory evidence of compliance with any continuing education requirements under this regulation for license renewal; or
Fails to submit the annual report required under Regulation .12 of this chapter.
If the renewal applicant fails to submit the required documents within 1 year of the renewal date, the status of the license shall be changed to nonrenewed.
The Board shall place a licensee on inactive status at the request of the licensee if the licensee submits to the Board:
A completed application for inactive status on the form required by the Board; and
The fee for inactive status specified in Regulation .18 of this chapter.
The Board shall reactivate the license of a licensee who has requested inactive status if the licensee:
Complies with any continuing education and data reporting requirements established by the Board for this purpose;
Pays to the Board a reactivation fee specified in Regulation .18 of this chapter; and
Is otherwise entitled to be licensed in accordance with this regulation.
The Board shall reinstate the license of an individual who has failed to renew the license for any reason if the individual:
Is otherwise entitled to be licensed in accordance with this regulation;
Complies with any continuing education and data reporting requirements established by the Board for this purpose;
Submits a completed application for reinstatement to the Board;
Pays to the Board the fee for reinstatement;
Completes a criminal history record check in accordance with Heath Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland, for a license that has expired or lapsed for more than 1 year; and
Applies to the Board for reinstatement of the license within 5 years after the license expires.

The Board may not reinstate the license of a licensed direct-entry midwife who fails to apply for reinstatement of the license within 5 years after the license expires. The individual may become licensed by meeting the current requirements for obtaining a new license as set forth in:
Health Occupations Article, §§8-6C-13 — 8-6C-16, Annotated Code of Maryland; and
This chapter.

A licensee shall submit to an additional criminal history records check every 12 years. The Board may not renew a license if the criminal history record information required by this section has not been received.
Criminal history records checks for renewal applicants shall be scheduled according to the licensee’s birth month as follows:
In 2027 — all applicants with a September and October birth month;
In 2029 — all applicants with a November and December birth month;
In 2031 — all applicants with a January and February birth month;
In 2033 — all applicants with a March and April birth month;
In 2035 — all applicants with a May and June birth month; and
In 2037 — all applicants with a July and August birth month.

section.heading: Requirements for Application for Initial Licensure.

para.text: An applicant for initial licensure as a certified midwife shall submit to the Board:
A completed application on the form that the Board requires;
Written, verified evidence that the applicant has met the requirements of Regulation .03C—E of this chapter;
Written, verified evidence that the applicant has submitted to a criminal history records check as required by Regulation .03B of this chapter by submitting:
One complete set of fingerprints, as required by the Central Repository and the Federal Bureau of Investigation; and
All fees required by the Central Repository and the FBI;

Any documentation requested from the applicant by the Board including, but not limited to, official certified or true test court documents and a signed, dated explanation written by the applicant, regarding the facts and circumstances, outcome, and current status of any criminal history record information received by the Board:
In accordance with Health Occupations Article, §8-303, Annotated Code of Maryland;
In an answer to a question on the Board’s application form; or
From any other source;
Any additional documentation requested by the Board if the documentation received from the applicant under §A(4) of this regulation is incomplete or insufficient; and
A fee for initial licensure as specified under Regulation .13 of this chapter.
If an application is not complete when initially submitted to the Board by the applicant, the applicant shall have no longer than 12 months from the date the application is received by the Board to:
Complete the application; and
Provide all information and documents required in §A of this regulation.

If an applicant fails to provide to the Board a complete application and any additional documentation requested by the Board in §A of this regulation within 12 months from the date the application is received by the Board, then the application:
Shall be considered abandoned; and
May be destroyed.
Once an application is deemed abandoned under §C of this regulation, an individual seeking licensure shall:
Submit a new application;
Meet all of the requirements for licensure; and
Pay the required fees in accordance with Regulation .13 of this chapter in effect at the time of re-application.

para.text: An MCO shall have sufficient provider capacity to provide health care services to Program recipients residing in a geographic region no smaller in size than one county or the City of Baltimore.
An MCO shall comply with COMAR 10.09.36.

An MCO shall enter a memorandum of understanding with each local health department in its service area addressing the method by which the MCO and the local health department will collaborate and communicate on matters of mutual interest and concern, including but not limited to the responsibility of the local health department for:
Contact tracing for sexually transmitted diseases; and
Directly observed therapy for tuberculosis.
Assurance Against Insolvency.
An MCO shall be actuarially sound.
An applicant shall possess an initial surplus in the amount of $1,500,000 as specified in Health-General Article, §15-102.4(a)(2)(ii), Annotated Code of Maryland.

If the Commissioner determines and reports to the Secretary that the applicant has an initial surplus that is at least $1,250,000 but less than $1,500,000, before approval the Department shall designate funds in trust sufficient to provide an initial surplus of $1,500,000.

If the Commissioner determines and reports to the Secretary that the applicant's initial surplus is less than $1,250,000 before approval the Department may, at its discretion, designate funds in trust in an amount equal to:

The sum of the amounts due to the owners of the applicant from the Department for Medicaid services provided on a fee-for-service basis, so long as the owners of the applicant have waived in writing their right to receive Medicaid payments until such time as the Department is permitted to remove its funds from the trust account pursuant to §D(6) of this regulation; or

If a financial guarantor with sufficient net worth and an adequate history of generating net income agrees to pay claims against the MCO in the case of insolvency, the difference between $1,250,000 and the applicant's initial surplus.

If, in accordance with §D(4) of this regulation, the Department designates funds sufficient to increase the applicants initial surplus to $1,250,000, the Department shall designate $250,000 in trust for the applicant.

Funds designated by the Secretary pursuant to §D(3)(5) of this regulation shall remain in trust until such time as the Commissioner has determined that the MCO meets the minimum statutory surplus requirements based on the MCOs annual report submitted pursuant to Insurance Article, §5-605, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Before approval of an applicant, the Secretary shall notify the Commissioner whether the Secretary has placed any money in trust under this section.
In the event of insolvency, the MCO shall cover continuation of services to enrollees for the duration of the period for which capitation payment has been made.
An MCO shall meet the solvency standards established by the State for private HMOs, or be licensed or certified by the State as a risk-bearing entity except if the MCO:
Is a public entity; or
Is, or is controlled by, one or more federally qualified health centers and meets the solvency standards established by the State for those centers;
Has its solvency guaranteed by the State.
Health Care Delivery. An MCO shall:
Provide the services set forth in COMAR 10.67.06 promptly and continuously, consistent with good medical practice and community professional standards;
Conform with and fulfill the requirements of 42 CFR §422.128, as amended, and provide adult enrollees with written information on advance directives which shall:
Include a description of applicable State law; and
Reflect a change in State law as soon as possible, but not later than 90 days after the effective date of the change.

Provide each enrollee within 10 days of notification to the MCO of the enrollee’s enrollment with a distinctive, durable identification card, clearly indicating the bearer to be a member of the MCO and containing, at a minimum:
The enrollee's Medicaid number;
The MCO's consumer services hotline telephone number;
The Department's enrollee hotline telephone number;
Enrollee's assigned primary care provider's name and telephone number; and
The Department’s name, logo, or other Department branding as approved by the Department;
Provide enrollees, within 30 days before the intended effective date, written notice when there is a significant change in the nature or location of services provided; and
Provide on the card required in §E(3) of this regulation, on a separate prescription benefit card, or other technology, prescription billing information that:

Complies with the standards set forth in the National Council for Prescription Drug Programs pharmacy ID card prescription benefit card implementation guide at the time of issuance of the card or other technology; or
Includes, at a minimum, the following data elements:
The name or identifying trademark of the MCO;
The name and identification number of the recipient;
The telephone number that providers may call for pharmacy benefit assistance;
The unique Medicaid-specific Bank Identification Number and Processor Control Number combination, along with group number identifiers, necessary for the participant to obtain pharmacy benefits; and
All additional electronic transaction routing information and other numbers required by the MCO or its pharmacy benefits manager to process a prescription claim electronically.
An MCO:
Shall comply with the standards in P.L. 101-336, Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, 42 U.S.C. §12101 et seq.;

May not discriminate against an enrollee on any basis, including, but not limited to, age, sex, race, creed, color, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, physical or mental handicap, health status, or need for health care services;
Shall prepare and make available all publications in a manner consistent with COMAR 10.67.05.01A, including, but not limited to:
Provider directories;
Enrollee handbooks;
Health education materials; and
Informational brochures.

An MCO shall maintain enrollee medical records in compliance with Health-General Article, §4-301 et seq., Annotated Code of Maryland, and the utilization control requirement of 42 CFR Part 456, as amended.

An MCO shall permit the enrollment of a waiver-eligible Program recipient who is enrolled by the Department or who selects the MCO, unless the MCO's enrollment meets or exceeds any enrollment limits mutually agreed to by the Department and the MCO.
MCO Local Access Area Participation.
Effective January 1, 2014, an MCO shall open in all local access areas located within the same county in which the MCO chooses to participate.
The MCO shall provide written notification to the Department of the MCO's intent to participate and accept new enrollees in each of the counties by September 15 for the next calendar year.

The MCO's decision to accept new enrollees is in effect from January 1 to December 31 unless the Department decides there is adequate justification to waive this requirement, which includes, but is not limited to, a rate cut or an MCO exit from the market.

Unless the Department approves a shorter time frame, an MCO that exits the Program during the calendar year shall submit their exit transition plan to the Department 120 days prior to the effective date of the exit.

If the MCO has not participated in a county for a period of 12 or more consecutive months, the MCO may participate and accept new enrollees in that county by notifying the Department at least 30 days before accepting new enrollees.
An MCO that voluntarily freezes for new enrollments in a county shall remain frozen in that county for the remainder of the calendar year and the following calendar year.
If system modifications require longer than 30 days to implement, the effective date may be extended.
The MCO shall follow the access standards specified in COMAR 10.67.05.06 and .05-1.
In counties where the MCO decides to stop accepting new enrollees, the MCO shall:
Continue to accept enrollees who regain eligibility within 120 days of becoming ineligible for the Program;
Accept newborns if the mother is an MCO member at the time of birth; and
Accept the family members of enrollees enrolled with the MCO before the effective date that the MCO stopped accepting new enrollees.

An HMO that is approved as an MCO and that requires its panel providers to participate in an MCO shall submit for review by the Secretary its plan to assure the equitable distribution of enrollees and to ensure that a provider is not assigned a disproportionate number of enrollees, as required by Health-General Article, §15-102.5, Annotated Code of Maryland.
An MCO shall comply with the provisions of Insurance Article, §15-112, Annotated Code of Maryland when credentialing providers, and during the credentialing process the MCO:
May not discriminate against particular providers that serve high-risk populations or specialize in conditions that require costly treatment;
May not employ or contract with providers excluded from participation in federal health care programs under either §1128 or 1128A of the Social Security Act; and
Shall give the affected providers written notice of the reason for its decision if the MCO declines to include the providers in its network.
The requirements of Regulation .17A(2) of this chapter, or §L(1) of this regulation, may not be construed to:
Require an MCO to contract with providers beyond the number necessary to meet the needs of its enrollees;
Preclude an MCO from using different reimbursement amounts:
For different specialties; or
For different practitioners in the same specialty; or
Preclude an MCO from establishing measures that are designed to maintain quality of services and control costs, consistent with its responsibilities to enrollees.
Disclosure of Provider Incentive Plans.
An MCO shall include, at a minimum, the provisions required by 42 CFR §438.3(i)(3) in all provider incentive plans.
An MCO shall disclose the provisions detailed in §N(1) of this regulation:
Prior to approval of its contract or agreement; and
Upon the contract's or agreement's anniversary or renewal effective date.

An MCO shall include in the disclosures required by §N(2) of this regulation information sufficient for the Department to determine whether the incentive plans meet the requirements of 42 CFR §438.3(i)(3) when there exist compensation arrangements under which payment for designated health services furnished to an individual on the basis of a physician referral would otherwise be denied under §1903(a) of the Social Security Act.
When making a referral, an MCO shall use the uniform consultation referral form adopted by the Maryland Insurance Administration at COMAR 31.10.12.06.
An MCO shall meet all other requirements of applicable State and federal law including but not limited to:
Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964;
Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 regarding education programs and activities;
The Age Discrimination Act of 1975;
The Rehabilitation Act of 1973;
Any laws regarding privacy and confidentiality;
Any laws that pertain to enrollee rights;
45 CFR Part 74, as amended, including particular attention to requirements at 45 CFR §§74.42, 74.43, 74.44, 74.48, and 74. 53(a) and (b), and Appendix A; and
Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act.
An MCO shall meet all program integrity requirements as set forth in COMAR 10.67.07.
The following applies to the Department's Health Home Program as described in COMAR 10.09.33:
The MCO may not provide services that duplicate the CMS reimbursed health home services for members participating in the State's Health Home Program;
The State shall inform the MCO of members assigned to the State's Health Home Program so that the MCO can prepare to coordinate care with the health homes;
The MCO shall provide a point of contact for the health homes to the State who shall share with all the enrolled health homes;
The MCO shall make referrals to the health homes of members who meet the criteria for enrollment in the program;
To facilitate this process, the State shall provide information to the MCO on all the enrolled health homes in the MCO's service areas; and
The MCO shall assist the health homes as necessary in accessing somatic care services for health home recipients.
Effective January 1, 2022, the Department shall establish the HealthChoice Population Health Incentive Program (PHIP).
An MCO may be eligible for an incentive payment for the following measures through measurement year 2025:
Ambulatory care visits for Supplemental Security Income (SSI) adults;
Ambulatory care visits for Supplemental Security Income (SSI) children;
HEDIS asthma medication ratio;
Hemoglobin A1c control for patients with diabetes — poor control (>9.0%);
Lead screening measures:
Lead screening measure for children 1223 months old; and
HEDIS lead screening in children;
HEDIS postpartum care;
HEDIS risk of continued opioid use >=31 days covered; and
HEDIS timeliness of prenatal care.
Effective measurement year 2026, an MCO may be eligible for an incentive payment for the following measures:
Child and adolescent well-care visits—total rate indicator;
Childhood immunization status—combination 3 indicator;
Colorectal cancer screening—total rate indicator;
Controlling high blood pressure;
Glycemic status assessment for patients with diabetes—Glycemic status >=9.0 percent indicator;
Immunizations for adolescents—combination 2 indicator;
Prenatal and postpartum care—timeliness of prenatal care indicator;
Well-child visits in the first 30 months of life—ages 0-15 months indicator; and
Well-child visits in the first 30 months of life—ages 15-30 months indicator.

Each measure identified in §B of this regulation shall be valued equally at a proportional share of available incentive funds, except for measures §B(5)(a) and (b), which are each valued at half of the available incentive funds relative to one of the other measures.
There shall be two rounds of potential incentive payments an MCO may earn.
Subject to budget approval, total PHIP funding shall be determined prior to the measurement year and included in the MCO contract.
All PHIP payments shall be funded independently from and outside of MCO capitation payments during a given calendar year.

Each MCO shall be eligible for no more than 1 percent of the plan's measurement year capitation payments, excluding supplemental payments outside of capitation, as total payment from round one and round two.

If the Department determines that the score for any measure identified in §B of this regulation may not be comparable to the previous year's score due to alterations in measure specifications or other factors, the Department may exclude the measure from the PHIP and adjust the incentive valuation in accordance with the remaining performance measures.
Round One Incentives.
An MCO may earn two types of incentives in round one:
A performance incentive payment; and
An improvement incentive payment.
If an MCO does not report a performance measure or an MCO has a performance score of 0 percent, then the MCO is awarded no performance or improvement incentive payments for this measure.
Performance Incentive Payments for Round One.
Performance incentive payments shall be based on the following categories for each performance measure:

Superlative performance, meaning the performance measure’s score is at or above the 90th percentile of HEDIS Medicaid performance nationwide during the prior measurement year, or estimated 90th percentile among Maryland HealthChoice MCO performance for non-HEDIS performance measures;

Very strong performance, meaning the performance measure’s score is between the 75th and 89th percentiles, inclusive, of HEDIS Medicaid performance nationwide during the prior measurement year, or between the estimated 75th and 89th percentiles, inclusive, among Maryland HealthChoice MCO performance for non-HEDIS performance measures; or

Strong performance, meaning the performance measure’s score is between the 50th and 74th percentiles, inclusive, of HEDIS Medicaid performance nationwide during the prior measurement year, or between the estimated 50th and 74th percentiles, inclusive, among Maryland HealthChoice MCO performance for non-HEDIS performance measures.
Payments for round one performance incentives shall be allocated as follows:
For superlative performance, an MCO may earn 100 percent of the incentive allocation for the performance measure;
For very strong performance, an MCO may earn 66.6 percent of the incentive allocation for the performance measure;
For strong performance, an MCO may earn 33.3 percent of the incentive allocation for the performance measure; and

Any MCO earning a performance measure score below the 50th percentile of HEDIS Medicaid performance nationwide during the prior measurement year on a HEDIS-based measure, or below the calculated 50th percentile among Maryland HealthChoice MCO performance for a non-HEDIS measure, shall be ineligible for a round one performance incentive payment.
Round One Improvement Incentive Payments.
An MCO may earn an improvement incentive payment of 33.3 percent of the incentive allocation for any performance measure if the following conditions are met:
The MCO demonstrates improvement of at least 0.5 percentage points in the measure compared to the previous measurement year; and

The performance measure score is at or above the 50th percentile of HEDIS Medicaid performance nationwide on a HEDIS-based measure, or the 50th percentile of Maryland HealthChoice MCO performance for a non-HEDIS measure.
An MCO earning a superlative performance incentive payment for a performance measure is ineligible for an improvement incentive payment for the same measure.
For any performance measures in which a lower score indicates stronger performance, year-over-year improvement is demonstrated by a reduction in the score for that measure.
If an MCO is missing or zero-valued for a performance measure in the previous year, then no improvement incentive will be awarded in the measurement year.
Round Two Incentive Payments.
An MCO may qualify for payments under round two if the following conditions are met:
For measurement years up to and including 2024:
The MCO earned above 80 percent of possible round one incentives; and
The MCO did not have penalties applied during the measurement year for failure to meet the HEDIS MCO Performance Monitoring Policy included in the MCO contract.
For measurement year 2025, the MCO earned above 80 percent of possible round one incentives; and
Effective measurement year 2026, the MCO earned above 75 percent of possible round one incentives.

Subject to budget approval, any remaining funds that were unallocated during round one may be awarded to eligible MCOs in round two for a maximum incentive award of up to 1 percent of its total capitation payment during the PHIP measurement year, excluding supplemental payments outside of capitation.

If any remaining funds that were unallocated during round one are not sufficient to settle all qualifying MCOs up to 1 percent of capitation in round two, then the leftover funds will be awarded proportionally among qualifying MCOs based on enrollment.
If additional funds remain after both round one and round two, the Department may, within its discretion, allocate the funding as follows:
Make additional payments to MCOs that are below 1 percent of capitation based on improvement or performance; or
Place remaining funds into a nonlapsing pool.

Effective measurement year 2025, an MCO with penalties under the HEDIS MCO Performance Monitoring Policy included in the HealthChoice MCO Agreement shall be excluded from all rounds of PHIP for that measurement year.
Incentives awarded under this regulation and exclusion from PHIP participation are not appealable under COMAR 10.67.10..

section.heading: Special Needs Populations — Individuals with HIV/AIDS.

para.text: An MCO shall meet the standards set forth in this regulation for treating individuals with HIV/AIDS.
HIV/AIDS Specialist.
An MCO shall allow an enrollee with HIV/AIDS to choose an HIV/AIDS specialist for treatment and coordination of primary and specialty care.
To qualify as an HIV/AIDS specialist, a health care provider shall be board certified in the field of infectious diseases by a member board of the American Board of Medical Specialties or:
Hold a current, valid, unrevoked, and unsuspended Maryland license or certification as a:
Doctor of medicine;
Doctor of osteopathy;
Nurse practitioner; or
Physician's assistant being supervised by a medical doctor;
Have provided direct, continuous, ongoing care for at least 20 patients with HIV over the past 2 years; and
Have completed one of the following requirements:

If a medical doctor, certified physician's assistant being supervised by a medical doctor, or doctor of osteopathy, at least 30 hours of HIV-related continuing medical education category I credits over the past 2 years;
If a nurse practitioner, at least 30 hours of HIV-related continuing education units over the past 2 years;
If a medical doctor, certified physician's assistant being supervised by a medical doctor, doctor of osteopathy, or a nurse practitioner, an accredited training program over the past year; or

If a medical doctor, certified physician's assistant being supervised by a medical doctor, doctor of osteopathy, or a nurse practitioner, has completed the American Academy of HIV Medicine (AAHIVM) credentialing examination.
AIDS Case Management Services.
An MCO shall ensure that an enrollee with HIV/AIDS receives case management services that:
Link the enrollee with the full range of available benefits;
Link the enrollee with any additional needed services including:
Mental health services;
Substance abuse services;
Medical services;
Social services;
Financial services;
Counseling services;
Educational services;
Housing services; and
Other required support services;
Ensure timely and coordinated access to medically necessary levels of care that support continuity of care across the continuum of service providers;

Are performed by licensed physicians, physician assistants, advanced practice nurses, registered nurses, social workers, or other individuals who are appropriately trained, experienced, and supervised by a licensed practitioner; and
Include, but are not limited to:

Initial and ongoing assessment of the enrollee's needs and personal support systems, including the MCO offering an enrollee one face-to-face meeting during the initial assessment and documenting the enrollee's acceptance or declination of the face to face meeting;
Development of a comprehensive, individualized service plan, using a multidisciplinary approach;
Coordination of the services required to implement the plan;
Periodic reevaluation and adaptation of the plan as necessary over the life of the enrollee;

Development of an outreach system for the enrollee and family by which the case manager and primary care provider track services received, clinical outcomes, and the need for additional follow-up; and
Serving as an effective enrollee advocate to resolve differences between the enrollee and providers of care pertaining to the course or content of therapeutic interventions.

An enrollee diagnosed with HIV/AIDS shall be offered case management services by the MCO at any time after diagnosis. An enrollee who has previously refused these services may request case management from the MCO at any time.
Diagnostic Evaluation Service (DES) Assessment.
An MCO shall offer a diagnostic evaluation service (DES) assessment annually and document the enrollee's acceptance or declination.
The DES shall consist of a comprehensive medical and psychosocial assessment.
A DES provider shall use assessment and care plan forms used by the Department for adult and pediatric assessments.
An individual shall select a DES provider from an approved list of sites, and may select a DES provider which is not part of the individual's MCO if so desired.
An MCO and other qualified institutions may become DES providers as provided in COMAR 10.09.32.03C.
An individual with HIV/AIDS who has a substance use disorder shall be referred to the behavioral health ASO for substance abuse treatment within 24 hours of request.
Clinical Trials.
An MCO may refer enrollees who are individuals with HIV/AIDS to facilities or organizations that can provide the enrollees' access to clinical trials.
An MCO shall provide enrollees with HIV/AIDS access to clinical trials in accordance with COMAR 10.67.06.26-1.

section.heading: MCO Payment for Self-Referred, Emergency, Physician, and Hospital Services.

para.text: MCO Payment for Self-Referred Services.

For undisputed claims that are submitted to the MCO within 6 months of the date of service, an MCO shall reimburse out-of-plan providers within 30 days for eligible services performed upon an enrollee who has self-referred:
To a school-based health clinic pursuant to COMAR 10.67.06.28B, for services described in COMAR 10.67.07;
For family planning services, pursuant to COMAR 10.67.06.28A;
For an initial medical examination for an enrollee who is a child in State-supervised care, pursuant to Regulation .13F of this chapter;
For one annual diagnostic and evaluation service visit for an enrollee diagnosed with human immunodeficiency virus or acquired immune deficiency syndrome (HIV/AIDS) pursuant to COMAR 10.67.06.28E;
For obstetric and gynecologic care provided to a pregnant woman, under the circumstances described in COMAR 10.67.06.28C; and
For an initial medical examination of a newborn when the:
Examination is performed in a hospital by an on-call physician; and
MCO failed to provide for the service before the newborn's discharge from the hospital.

An MCO shall reimburse out-of-plan providers to whom enrollees have self-referred for school-based services as described in COMAR 10.67.07.03 and family planning services including office visits (CPT codes 9920199205 and 9921199215), preventive medicine office visits (CPT codes 9938399386 and 9939399396), and all FDA-approved contraceptive devices, methods and supplies, at the established Medicaid rates.

An MCO shall reimburse out-of-plan providers to whom enrollees have self-referred for an initial examination for a child in State-supervised care utilizing the Medicaid payment schedule for the following procedure codes:

tr.th: Periodic Comprehensive or Preventive Services (Established Patient)

para.text: An MCO shall reimburse out-of-plan providers rendering pregnancy-related services, as described in COMAR 10.67.06.28, at the Medicaid rate.
An MCO shall reimburse out-of-plan providers performing the DES for HIV/AIDS at the Medicaid rate.

An MCO may require enrollees to utilize in-plan providers for pharmacy and laboratory services ordered by out-of-plan providers of self-referral services, except as provided in §A(7) of this regulation.
An MCO shall reimburse out-of-plan providers at the Medicaid rate for medically necessary pharmacy and laboratory services when the pharmacy or laboratory service is provided:
In connection with a self-referred service specified in §A(1) of this regulation; and
On-site by the out-of-plan provider at the same location that the self-referred service specified in §A(1) of this regulation was delivered to the MCO's enrollee.

An MCO shall reimburse out-of-plan providers for renal dialysis services in a Medicare-certified facility, at least the Medicaid rate, regardless of whether or not the MCO's preauthorization was secured.

An MCO shall reimburse out-of-plan providers under the circumstances described in COMAR 10.67.06.28G at a rate not less than the fee-for-service Medicaid rate for an initial medical examination of a newborn when the mother's MCO fails to provide for the service before the newborn is discharged from the hospital.
An MCO shall reimburse out-of-plan providers at the Medicaid fee-for-service rate for services performed in a free-standing birth center as described in COMAR 10.67.06.28.

An MCO shall reimburse out-of-plan doulas at the Medicaid fee-for-service rate for services performed during the prenatal, labor and delivery, and postpartum periods of pregnancy as described in COMAR 10.67.06.28 through December 31, 2026.

MCO Payment for Emergency Services Provided at a Hospital. An MCO shall reimburse a hospital emergency facility and provider, which is not required to obtain prior authorization or approval for payment from an MCO in order to obtain reimbursement under this regulation, for:
Health care services that meet the definition of emergency services in Health-General Article, §19-701, Annotated Code of Maryland;
Medical screening services rendered to meet the requirements of the federal Emergency Medical Treatment and Active Labor Act;

Medically necessary services if the MCO authorized, referred, or otherwise instructed the enrollee to use the emergency facility and the medically necessary services are related to the emergency condition; and

Medically necessary services that relate to the condition presented and that are provided by the provider in the emergency facility to the enrollee if the MCO fails to provide 24-hour access to a physician.
MCO Payment to an Out-of-Network Federally Qualified Health Center for Services Immediately Required Due to an Unforeseen Illness, Injury, or Condition.

Effective October 1, 2010, an MCO shall reimburse an out-of-network federally qualified health center (FQHC) for services provided to an enrollee that are immediately required due to an unforeseen illness, injury, or condition if:
The FQHC participates in the Medical Assistance Program;
The FQHC does not have a contract with the MCO;
The services are immediately required due to the enrollee's unforeseen illness, injury, or condition;
The emergent services are provided on site at the FQHC; and

The FQHC has, before rendering services, verified with the enrollee's primary care provider that the enrollee cannot be seen within a reasonable amount of time based on the severity of the enrollee's condition.

An MCO may require that the FQHC provide documentation that the FQHC has obtained the verification required under §C(1)(e) of this regulation. An MCO is not required to reimburse an out-of-network FQHC for emergent services provided to an enrollee if the FQHC fails to provide the documentation.

An MCO may require that the FQHC provide documentation that services were required for the reasons identified under §C(1)(c) of this regulation. An MCO is not required to reimburse an out-of-network FQHC for emergent services provided to an enrollee if the FQHC fails to provide the documentation.
The rate at which the MCO shall reimburse an out-of-network FQHC for services provided under §C(1) of this regulation shall be the rate identified in COMAR 10.67.04.21.
For any reimbursement paid by an MCO under §C of this regulation, the Program shall pay the MCO the difference between the rates identified in COMAR 10.67.04.21 and COMAR 10.09.08.05-1.
MCO Payment for Provider Services.
An MCO shall pass on to providers any MCO rate adjustment that is specified by the Department for a fee increase.
For inpatient services performed in hospitals, an MCO shall pay all providers, regardless of the provider's contracting status, at least the Medicaid fee-for-service rate.
The MCO may not be required to pay providers more than the Medicaid fee-for-service rate.
Payment for Hospital Services.
An MCO shall reimburse Maryland hospital providers on the basis of rates approved by the Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC).
An MCO shall reimburse hospital administrative days at the Medicaid fee-for-service rate.

Upon the direction of the Department, an MCO shall reduce payments by 20 percent to a hospital located in a contiguous state or in the District of Columbia for services rendered to its enrollees, if the hospital has failed to supply appropriate discharge data to the Health Services Cost Review Commission.

section.heading: Payments to Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHC).

para.text: FQHC’s shall be reimbursed under the Alternative Payment System (APS).
The Department shall:
Pay the MCO a prospective payment based on encounter data; and
Reconcile the prospective amount paid to the MCO with the MCO's actual expenditure amount, after receipt of MCO encounter data; and
MCOs shall reimburse any contracted FQHC, the FQHC’s rate established in accordance with COMAR 10.09.08.05-1A.

For self-referred services described in Regulation .20 of this chapter, the MCO shall pay the FQHC’s usual rate in accordance with §A of this regulation, regardless of the FQHC’s contracted status with the MCO.
